label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl, models/chumtoad.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: All ten views in sides.png show a plain rectangular box: rectangles from front, left, back, right, top and below, and a cuboid in the four corner views. The brief asks for a low six-legged crawler with a ring of teeth. There are no legs, no body shape and no mouth, so the outline does not match the brief's words in any view.

M2.reason: Measured 12 x 10 x 6. The brief gives no number, only 'the size of a headcrab', so there is no measured target (sizeAsked null). In lineup.png the box (C) is in the range of the small creatures but is much smaller than A. The volume is about right, but nothing confirms it is within 15% of headcrab size.

M3.reason: None of the parts the brief names are there: no six legs, no ring of teeth, no separate belly. It is a single box with nothing attached.

M4.reason: The whole thing is one flat mid grey in every view. It is not grey-green, it has no pale belly (the view from below is the same grey, only darker), and it does not look wet.

M5.reason: There is no surface detail: no wet sheen, no teeth, no belly line, no markings. There is only a faint mottled grey texture and light edge highlights on the box faces.

M6.reason: In lineup.png, C is plainly a grey box set beside three real creature models with shape, colour and legs. No player would take it for one of Half-Life's creatures.

M7.reason: A box has no front, so there is no front to judge. In the first walk frame of run.png the bottom of the box sits below the floor line, so it does not stand on its origin as a creature would.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. It has 12 triangles, far under twice a headcrab-sized creature's median. The box is closed, not inside out, and not floating in its rest pose. The measurement allows a 2 and nothing in the pictures argues against it for this item.

C1.reason: There are no parts to move. In run.png the box slides rigidly and its lower part sits below the floor line in every walk frame (0 to 34). In attack.png the whole box tumbles as one rigid block through the jump. Nothing walks or bites, and it sinks into the floor.

C2.reason: Measured: it keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts, so the game's headcrab code can play it.
